items.t: Forest Glen is the Burnaby South sub-area between Metrotown and Edmonds, framed by Kingsway, Willingdon Avenue, Bond Street and Nelson Avenue, mixing the Kingsway condo corridor with detached residential streets. It is named for Forest Glen Park at 4855 Bond Street.

Where the condos are: in two places. One is the towers on Hazel Street at the edge of Metrotown; the other is the older low-rises and towers on Nelson Avenue, McMurray Avenue and Sanders Street toward Burnaby South Secondary. The streets in between are detached houses.

Schools: Clinton Elementary (5858 Clinton Street), École Inman (3963 Brandon Street), Nelson Elementary (4850 Irmin Street), École Marlborough (6060 Marlborough Avenue) and Burnaby South Secondary (5455 Rumble Street).

Transit: route 110 runs on Bond Street and Nelson Avenue themselves (Metrotown–Lougheed via Willingdon, Deer Lake Parkway, Winston and Government) — the sub-area's own streets carry the bus, not just its edges.
Anchors: Wesburn Community Centre at 4781 Parkwood Avenue; Burnaby Hospital sits immediately north-east of the sub-area.
Planning: the Cascade Heights Community Plan was adopted in March 2025.

blocks.text: Good to know about Forest Glen BS condos

items.t: The "-bs" is a filing tag, not a place. "Forest Glen BS" is the MLS's Burnaby South designation; the park, schools and streets all just say Forest Glen. Searches and document requests that include "BS" as a name will miss records.

One building holds a fifth of the sub-area's identity. Sussex's 321 suites (41 storeys, built 2022) make it larger than several of the 1980s–90s Hazel towers combined; sub-area listing counts skew toward it whenever its owners list in number.

The hospital is the sub-area's north-east neighbour. Burnaby Hospital (3935 Kincaid Street, Fraser Health) sits immediately north-east of Forest Glen, and the Edmonds Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at #201-7315 Edmonds Street — the two care anchors for the whole Metrotown-to-Edmonds band.

items.t: Nearby areas: Metrotown to the west, Central Park and Patterson to the west and south-west, Burnaby Hospital and Cascade Heights to the north-east, Edmonds and South Slope to the east and south-east, and Deer Lake to the north.

The ground-level attached homes here are the townhouse-style units in the Oakwood strata on Denbigh Avenue, and new small strata multiplexes and duplexes on the house streets (Buxton, Elgin, Dufferin and Charlotte Court).

Transit and roads: Metrotown Station and Patterson Station (both Expo Line) are at the area's west side, and route 110 runs on Bond and Nelson streets themselves, between Metrotown Station and Lougheed Station via Willingdon, Deer Lake Parkway, Royal Oak, Gilpin, Sprott, Sperling Station, Winston, Government and Eastlake. Kingsway, Willingdon Avenue and Imperial Street are the main roads.

SD41 schools on the Province's list in or beside the area include Clinton Elementary (K–7), 5858 Clinton St, École Inman Elementary (K–7), 3963 Brandon St, Nelson Elementary (K–7), 4850 Irmin St, and École Marlborough Elementary (K–7), 6060 Marlborough Ave, with Burnaby South Secondary (8–12), 5455 Rumble St, to the south-east.

Parks and landmarks: Forest Glen Park (4855 Bond Street), which the area is named for; Deer Lake Park (6450 Deer Lake Avenue) to the north; Wesburn Community Centre (4781 Parkwood Avenue) on the south side; Burnaby Hospital (3935 Kincaid Street) just northeast; and Metrotown, one of Burnaby's four town centres, just west.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Forest Glen BS

items.t: For the Oakwood strata and each small strata project, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. In a four-unit strata the package is short, so read all of it, including who the other owners are and how much is actually in the reserve.

Depreciation reports in small stratas: since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must get a depreciation report every five years and can't vote to skip it. Oakwood is well over that; a four-unit strata on Buxton or Elgin isn't, so no report is required and you'll need your own building inspection instead. At least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve each year, which in a four-unit strata adds up to very little.

Taxes and rebates on a new home, such as the 2026 Buxton, Elgin and Dufferin multiplexes: property transfer tax is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% up to $2 million and 3% above, plus another 2% on the residential part above $3 million. First-time buyers are exempt on the first $500,000 for homes up to $835,000 (partial up to $860,000), and the newly built home exemption is full up to $1,100,000 and ends at $1,150,000. The first-time buyers' GST rebate (law since March 13, 2026) covers all the GST up to $1 million (maximum $50,000), phasing out at $1.5 million, for agreements from March 20, 2025 to 2031; the GST New Housing Rebate is 36% up to $6,300 (phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000). The Home Buyers' Plan allows $60,000, an FHSA $8,000 a year up to $40,000, and CMHC premiums run 0.6%–4.5%. 5% GST applies to new homes like these multiplexes, not resales, and the new-home warranty on a four-unit strata is worth checking separately.

blocks.text: Good to know about Forest Glen BS townhomes

items.t: The bus runs on the house streets. Route 110 goes through the north side of the area via Willingdon, Bond, Nelson, Bennett and Bonsor to Metrotown Station, along the same Bond and Nelson streets as Forest Glen Park and the detached houses, and to Sperling and Lougheed stations in the other direction. So the house streets have transit in both directions, not just the towers.

Watch the new four-lot stratas. A buyer at a 2026 Buxton or Elgin project gets strata ownership without a required depreciation report (those start at five lots), a contingency reserve fund built on 10% of a small budget, and three neighbours whose votes decide every major repair. None of that shows in a listing that just says "townhouse".

The zoning bylaw most guides still cite no longer exists. Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) repealed and replaced the 1965 bylaw effective July 1, 2026, and repackaged the districts into a height-based framework — any Forest Glen document quoting 1965-bylaw district numbers is quoting repealed law.

The park is small; the name is big. The sub-area takes its name from Forest Glen Park at 4855 Bond St, a neighbourhood park on the City's parks list — the larger green spaces buyers picture (Central Park west, Deer Lake Park north) sit at or beyond the sub-area's edges.

items.t: The new small multiplexes are stratified units on former house lots under the R1 zone. Check each project's strata plan and Form B; none of them is vacant land.

The only sourced size figures are the R1 SSMUH thresholds in (280 m² / 281 m²), which are zoning thresholds, not a claim about any existing lot's size. Kingsway corridor parcels are not R1 — confirm the zone parcel by parcel.

Serviced position: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable and a garbage toter fee, with the detached single-family water charge at $652.33 and sewer for single-family homes billed as a sewer parcel tax — the established streets sit inside that municipal system on the City's wording.
ALR: I don't know of any ALR land in Forest Glen. Check a specific property with the Agricultural Land Commission.

items.t: Forest Glen is in south Burnaby between Metrotown and Edmonds, around Kingsway, Willingdon Avenue, Bond Street and Nelson Avenue, named for Forest Glen Park (4855 Bond Street). It mixes the Kingsway towers and condos with detached streets south and east of Metrotown. Listings use "Forest Glen BS", where BS stands for Burnaby South.
Nearby areas: Metrotown west, Central Park and Patterson west and south-west, Burnaby Hospital and Cascade Heights north-east, Edmonds and South Slope east and south-east, Deer Lake north.

Main roads: Kingsway, Willingdon Avenue and Imperial Street, with Canada Way to the north-east and Marine Drive / Marine Way to the south. Transit: Metrotown Station and Patterson Station (both Expo Line) are at the west side, and route 110 runs on Bond and Nelson streets themselves between Metrotown Station and Lougheed Station via Willingdon, Deer Lake Parkway, Winston and Government Road — the house streets carry the bus, not just the corridor.

Nearby: Forest Glen Park (4855 Bond Street); Wesburn Community Centre (4781 Parkwood Avenue), with a large activity room, open by arrangement; and Deer Lake Park (6450 Deer Lake Avenue) to the north. Burnaby Hospital (3935 Kincaid Street) borders the area's northeast side, and the Edmonds Urgent and Primary Care Centre (#201-7315 Edmonds Street) is to the east.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Forest Glen

items.t: New small stratas: read the specific project's disclosure statement or Form B and its warranty enrolment, not the marketing.

Strata rules (for any bare-land strata lot and the small strata multiplexes): check the Form B (fees, amounts owing, levies, contingency reserve balance and insurance; within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page). Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years (a four-unit project usually doesn't; check the plan), and at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve. Rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited), and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.

If a parcel is in the ALR: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an extra residence can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). For farm class, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.

items.t: The community centre has no front desk: Wesburn Community Centre (4781 Parkwood Ave) has no regular office hours or staff onsite and visits are by arrangement — a small, checkable detail that surprises buyers pricing the south side's amenity.

faq.a: For records, strata documents and comparable searches, use the MLS classification — and check both names.
faq.q: Are the Hazel Street towers Metrotown or Forest Glen?

faq.a: Newest: Sussex (4711 Hazel Street), by Townline, built in 2022, 41 storeys and 321 homes. Oldest I've confirmed: Sanders Court (5025 Sanders Street), built in 1984, fully rainscreened in 2007 with a new roof in 2018. With 38 years between them, the questions are about warranty at one end and the age of the building envelope at the other.
faq.q: What is the newest building, and the oldest?

faq.a: Published positions vary and are bylaw questions, not law: current unit records show pets "Yes With" restrictions at Sussex and The Sovereign, "Cats OK" at The Newmark, and "No" at The Dynasty, Crystal Place and The Evergreen. Pet bylaws remain enforceable in BC — the registered bylaws on the Form B govern the specific building.
faq.q: Can I have a dog in the Hazel towers?

faq.a: It is treated here as one complex with two towers: 6070 McMurray Avenue (built 1987) and 6055 Nelson Avenue (built 1988, "La Mirage II").
faq.q: La Mirage has two addresses — is it one strata?

faq.a: A share-sale building, not a condo: the listing itself states buyers need all cash or 35% down through a specific credit union. Irving Apartments Ltd.
faq.q: A listing at 5127 Irving Street looks cheap for the area — what is it?

faq.a: Strata, according to listings: the 5115 Buxton Street project is listed as freehold strata (half duplex), and the fourplex at 5091 Buxton Street is marketed the same way. Four-lot stratas are below the five-lot threshold for a required depreciation report, so checking the building's condition is up to the buyer.
faq.q: The new Buxton Street fourplex — strata or not?

faq.a: Yes under provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw — read the registered bylaws in the Form B package.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Forest Glen strata home long-term?

faq.a: Both, with more condos: in September 2026 there were 64 condos and townhomes for sale and 6 sold, against 18 detached houses for sale and 1 sold. There are more condos and townhomes on and off Kingsway than houses on the house streets (SnapStats, September 2026)
